plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, the 6-date timeline completes: 1638 (Galileo records the 32-foot suction-pump limit in Florence) · Jun 1644 (Evangelista Torricelli & Vincenzo Viviani create the 30-inch mercury barometer and first sustained vacuum) · 19 Sep 1648 (Florin Périer's Puy-de-Dôme mountain climb for Blaise Pascal proves air pressure drops with altitude) · 8 May 1654 (Otto von Guericke's 16-horse Magdeburg hemispheres demonstration at Regensburg) · 1660–1662 (Robert Boyle & Robert Hooke prove sound vanishes in a vacuum and formulate Boyle's Law) · 1712 (Thomas Newcomen's atmospheric vacuum engine launches the Industrial Revolution), alongside Newcomen's 21-inch cylinder where cold water condenses steam into a vacuum so 14.7 psi outside air slams the piston down with >5 tonnes of force.

teach_overlay.scale: when cold water condensed the steam inside Newcomen's cylinder, the outside atmosphere slammed the piston down with over five tonnes of force twelve times a minute
